entry.other: General Security checks every name against border alerts (stop orders) for court cases, warrants or family-court matters.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Both the USD and the Lebanese Pound (also known as the Lebanese Lira) are accepted. Currency exchange facilities and ATMs are widely available in Beirut and other large cities. Daily withdrawal limits and high withdrawal fees may apply. Make sure you have access to enough hard currency cash during your stay. Contact your bank and monitor media reports before you travel to Lebanon. - Scams that affect travellers

laws.rule: All family law matters are based on local religious laws. This includes child custody and divorce decisions. If you're involved in custody or other family disputes, speak to a lawyer before you leave Australia. Ask for advice on how religious law may affect your family circumstances. Lebanon has not signed the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction. There are significant limits on our ability to assist in returning a child to Australia if they have been abducted by a parent. We can't intervene in local legal matters, including custody disputes. laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe and include mandatory jail terms. - Carrying or using drugs
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Serious crimes like murder and treason may result in life imprisonment with aggravated hard labour. Access to some areas of Lebanon is restricted. Authorities may detain you and take your camera if you photograph or film: military personnel or facilities government buildings major civilian infrastructure (such as power stations)
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Same-sex relations are illegal in Lebanon. Penalties include jail terms of up to one year. There's been an increase in anti-LGBTQIA+ rhetoric in the community. Some incidents of targeted harassment have occurred. - Advice for LGBTQIA+ travellers
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ information

laws.rule: The Islamic holiday month of Ramadan is observed in Lebanon. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws during this time. Avoid eating, drinking or smoking in public, or in front of people who are fasting.
laws.heading: Ramadan

laws.rule: Shortages of pharmaceuticals and medical supplies can occur without notice.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Standards of dress and behaviour are modest in parts of Lebanon, particularly at religious sites. Take care not to offend. If in doubt, seek local advice. Public displays of affection may cause offence in conservative and religious areas. Some hotels ask for proof of marriage before renting rooms to couples. Hotels may refuse you accommodation if you can't provide proof.
